f.histoire: Roses have been grown for about 5,000 years, first in China and Persia. The Greeks and Romans offered them to the goddess of love, Aphrodite (Venus). Ever since, the red rose has been the symbol of passionate love.
f.pousse: Wild roses grow all across the northern hemisphere. Today, florist roses mostly come from Kenya, Ecuador, Colombia and the Netherlands.
entretien: Re-cut the stems at an angle, about 2 cm, with a clean knife.
Remove any leaves that sit in the water.
Use a clean vase, fresh water and a flower food sachet if you have one.
Change the water every 2 days.
Keep it away from sun, heaters and fruit (fruit makes flowers wilt).
It lasts about 7 to 10 days.
f.parfum: It varies: many florist roses have little scent, while old garden roses smell wonderful.
f.allergenes: Little pollen, rarely causes allergies. Watch out for the thorns, they prick! Safe for cats and dogs.

f.histoire: The tulip comes from the mountains of Central Asia. The Ottoman sultans adored it, and then it reached the Netherlands in the 16th century. In 1637, a single bulb could cost as much as a house: this was "tulip mania".
f.pousse: It grows from a bulb, in countries with cold winters. The Netherlands produces billions of them every year.
entretien: Cold water, not too high in the vase.
Cut the stems straight across.
It keeps growing in the vase and bends toward the light: that's normal.
Don't put it with freshly cut daffodils (their sap harms it).
It lasts about 5 to 7 days.
f.parfum: Very light, almost nothing for most varieties.
f.allergenes: The bulb can irritate the skin of people who handle a lot of them. The bulb is toxic to cats and dogs.

f.histoire: The lily has been grown for more than 3,000 years: you can already see it in frescoes from ancient Crete. It is the symbol of purity, and the fleur-de-lis decorated the coat of arms of the kings of France.
f.pousse: It grows from a bulb in the temperate regions of Asia, Europe and North America.
entretien: Remove the stamens (the orange pollen) as soon as they open, using a tissue: this avoids stains.
Re-cut the stem at an angle.
Remove faded flowers: the buds will keep opening.
It lasts 1 to 2 weeks.
f.parfum: Very strong and sweet, especially oriental lilies. It can be overwhelming in a small room.
f.allergenes: Its pollen stains and can irritate. VERY DANGEROUS FOR CATS: the whole plant, the pollen and even the vase water can damage their kidneys. Keep it away from cats.

f.histoire: The sunflower comes from the Americas: Native American peoples grew it more than 4,000 years ago. The Spanish brought it back to Europe in the 16th century, and Van Gogh made it famous. When young, its flower follows the sun; when grown, it faces east.
f.pousse: In the sun, in warm regions. Ukraine and Russia grow the most, mainly for oil.
entretien: Its head is heavy: choose a tall, stable vase.
It drinks a lot: top up the water often.
Re-cut the stems at an angle and remove any leaves in the water.
It lasts about 6 to 10 days.
f.allergenes: Rarely causes allergies, but it belongs to the same family as chamomile and ragweed: be careful if you are allergic to those plants. Safe for pets.

f.histoire: Its name comes from the Greek "margarites", meaning pearl. Since forever, people have plucked its petals while saying "he loves me, a little, a lot, passionately, madly, not at all".
f.pousse: In meadows and along paths, in the sun, in Europe and Asia. It is also found in America, where it has spread.
entretien: Change the water every 2 days: it turns cloudy quickly.
Re-cut the stems and remove any leaves in the water.
It lasts about 7 to 10 days.
f.allergenes: Asteraceae family: it can irritate the skin or cause hay fever in sensitive people. Can cause digestive upset in cats and dogs if they eat it.

f.histoire: It is one of the biggest plant families: about 28,000 species. Vanilla is an orchid! In the 19th century, English collectors travelled to the ends of the earth to find them: this was called "orchidelirium".
f.pousse: All over the world, but mostly in tropical forests, often clinging to trees. Bouquet orchids come largely from Thailand and the Netherlands.
entretien: As cut flowers, they last a long time: 2 to 3 weeks.
Lukewarm water, and re-cut the stem now and then.
Avoid cold drafts and fruit.
In a pot: water once a week by soaking the pot, in light but no direct sun.
f.parfum: Most have little scent, but some species smell wonderful (sometimes of vanilla).
f.allergenes: Very rarely causes allergies: its pollen doesn't fly around. The moth orchid is safe for cats and dogs.

f.histoire: The Romans put lavender in their baths; its name is thought to come from the Latin "lavare", to wash. It has scented laundry for centuries, and its purple fields are the symbol of Provence.
f.pousse: In the sun, on dry, poor soils, around the Mediterranean. Provence, Bulgaria and England grow a lot of it.
entretien: Fresh: very little water in the vase.
To dry it: hang the bouquet upside down in a dark, dry place for 1 to 2 weeks.
Dried, it keeps its scent for several months.
f.allergenes: Its essential oil can irritate the skin. The pollen can bother sensitive people. The essential oil is dangerous for cats: keep it away from them.

f.histoire: In China, it is called "the queen of flowers": emperors were already growing it more than 1,500 years ago. Its name comes from Paeon, the physician of the Greek gods.
f.pousse: In countries with cold winters. A single peony plant can live for more than 50 years.
entretien: Buy it as a bud, soft to the touch.
Ants on the buds? They're harmless: just rinse them off.
Fresh water. It opens in 1 to 3 days, then lasts 5 to 7 days.
In a cool place, it lasts longer.
f.parfum: Often sweet, rosy or lemony depending on the variety.
f.allergenes: Moderate pollen. Can cause digestive upset in cats, dogs and horses if they eat it.

f.histoire: Jasmine comes from the Himalayas and South Asia. It is the national flower of the Philippines and Indonesia. In China, tea is scented with its flowers, and in Grasse it is picked at dawn for the great perfumes.
f.pousse: In warm regions, climbing up walls. India and Egypt produce the most for perfumery.
entretien: As cut flowers, it is fragile: 1 to 3 days. It is often made into garlands.
Keep it cool and mist it with a little water.
In a pot: lots of light and a cool winter so that it blooms again.
f.parfum: Very intense and sweet, even stronger in the evening.
f.allergenes: Its very strong scent can cause headaches or bother people with asthma. True jasmine is safe for pets (careful: "Carolina jasmine" is not a jasmine and is very toxic).

f.histoire: It is the flower of the islands: national flower of Malaysia, symbol of Hawaii. In Polynesia, it is worn behind the ear. In the Caribbean, the "sorrel" hibiscus makes the red Christmas drink, and bissap in Senegal.
f.pousse: In tropical regions: Caribbean, Pacific, Asia. Each flower lives only one day, but the plant makes new ones all the time.
entretien: Once cut, the flower lasts just one day, even without water.
Lay it on a table or float it in a bowl of water.
In a pot: lots of sun, regular watering, protected from the cold (not below 10 °C).
f.allergenes: Very rarely causes allergies. Garden hibiscus from the tropics is generally safe for cats and dogs.
